A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same P2SAM research despite the title change. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 includes appendices A–F, which were included in the assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original medical and natural-image segmentation experiments, quantitative ablations and qualitative results in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds tracking comparisons, interactive-segmentation experiments, part-segmentation results and a cell-segmentation case study.

M1.justification: The core clustering, cosine-similarity prompt selection and distribution-based retrieval remain unchanged. Appendix E adds task-specific adaptations: extra negative prompts for part segmentation and previous-frame bounding-box regularization for cell segmentation. Appendix B's fuller adaptation recipe documents an existing procedure without establishing that it changed between versions.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds distinct task coverage: one-shot part segmentation on PASCAL-Part and segmentation among similar cells on PhC-C2DH-U373. Table 12 also adds interactive point/box-prompt evaluation on Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB. These extend the tested target granularity, population and input requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds comparisons with MedSAM, label propagation, AOT, SAM 2 and GF-SAM. Conversely, Painter, SegGPT, SEEM and PerSAM-F disappear from the corresponding natural-image comparison, and PerSAM-F model-size comparisons are removed. The new CVC baseline in Table 3 has ambiguous attribution: Section 4.2 identifies Sanderson and Matuszewski's method, while Appendix E identifies DuckNet.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce substantially different controls and information budgets: MedSAM receives boxes at each visit, Table 12 varies manual prompt availability, Table 11 compares pretraining initializations, and Appendix E evaluates temporal box regularization. The original splits, training epochs, batch size and optimizer settings remain unchanged. Newly disclosed retrieval ranges do not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: The original quantitative ablations are retained. Appendices D–E add visual analyses of how varying part counts divide medical and natural objects, a pretraining-initialization comparison, interactive-prompt controls, an extra-negative-prompt ablation for part segmentation, and a similar-cell failure case with and without box regularization. These investigate additional mechanisms and applicability limits.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the matched original ablation scores are unchanged, but substantial results are added and comparator entries removed. New results include SAM 2 versus SAM 2 plus P2SAM at 81.98 versus 84.43 on CVC-ClinicDB, and P2SAM versus Matcher at 32.24 versus 33.66 mIoU on PASCAL-Part. Table 5's unadapted P2SAM CVC score of 67.23 differs unexplained from Table 2's 66.45; this is not an established performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies the feature-distribution transport objective, including cosine-similarity costs and marginal constraints, beyond v1's unspecified Wasserstein computation. As printed, minimizing cosine similarity appears inconsistent with the intended distribution-matching interpretation. Other equation changes largely formalize existing operations; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain one-shot adaptation without patient-specific fine-tuning, part-aware prompting with retrieval, broad applicability, and the same headline medical and PerSeg results. Explicit SAM 2 support exemplifies the earlier claim of compatibility with point-promptable models. The broader title does not substantially redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands qualifications and interpretation. It identifies medical parts as data-driven, acknowledges weaker part-segmentation performance and failure among similar instances, explains the benefit of temporal regularization, and discusses the information advantage of manual boxes. It also develops arguments about pretraining choices, tracking suitability and the smaller advantage over PerSAM after medical adaptation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C supply important details absent from the supplied v1: LoRA placement and trainable components, no-prompt training, stopped embedding gradients, single-mask output, dataset/backbone-specific prompt ranges and their selection procedure. The abstract changes a promised code release to a concrete repository link. These improve documentation without proving that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix E substantially expand positioning against interactive medical segmentation and tracking. Added discussions include SAM 2, its medical successor, ScribblePrompt, One-Prompt, UniverSeg and GF-SAM, with explanations of comparator selection and differences from P2SAM. Some earlier general vision citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Terminology changes from patient-specific to patient-adaptive segmentation, and P2SAM's expanded name changes. Ablations precede qualitative results, related work gains a separate medical-segmentation discussion, and supporting material is organized into six appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a journal layout, reorganizes tables into paired displays, reduces the natural-image comparison table and adds several experimental and implementation tables. Figures receive revised labels and captions; Figure 4 substitutes a polyp example while retaining the robot example in Appendix D. Additional part visualizations and the cell-segmentation figure substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The adaptation recipe and prompt ranges absent from the supplied v1 make v2 easier to reproduce, while new controls and failure cases improve assessment of applicability. These gains are tempered by removal of strong natural-image comparators, inconsistent baseline attribution and the unexplained Table 5 score. Appendix F also introduces a problematic objective that minimizes cosine similarity. The added transparency and analysis support a limited net improvement, with these technical and reporting issues restricting the gain.
